title: Fit the spring clamp on the glass filter holder and test the joint with a low lift
instruction:
Grip the funnel's upper cylinder. Centre it over the membrane on the frit (porous support disc), lower it straight down and hold it steady. With the other gripper, squeeze the spring clamp handles, slide the jaws over both flanges (glass rims), let them close and move that gripper clear.

Lift straight up from the mark by the upper cylinder alone. Keep the flask over the padded tray through set-down. Hold the foot's lowest edge between the blue stripe's top and the gauge top for the time given in Scoring. Never lift higher. Stop lifting if the flanges separate. If glass breaks, stop and leave fragments in the tray. Set the flask upright on its mark, release the funnel and keep both grippers clear for the time given in Scoring.

After the trial, film the joint. With intact glass, support the flask in the tray and steady the funnel. Squeeze the handles, remove the clamp and lift the funnel straight off. Film the membrane before touching it. Check that it is intact and centred.
context: A lab technician assembling a glass vacuum filter holder uses this dry lift to check that the spring clamp holds both flanges together under the weight of the empty filtering flask.
setup: On the bench, put a stable, padded tray with raised sides under the whole lift area to catch a dropped flask and contain fragments. Put the flask's mark on the pad. Check that both grippers can reach the parts and withdraw without striking the tray rim. Stand the empty, dry 1 L flask upright on its mark with the side arm pointing away from the robot. Check that the stopper holds the base securely in the flask. Centre a fresh, dry 47 mm membrane on the frit. Set the height gauge beside the flask and zero it at the surface that supports the resting flask foot. Keep the lowest edge of the foot, the blue stripe and the gauge top visible from the side. Stand the 300 mL funnel on its flange on the clean wipe to the left. Lay the closed spring clamp flat on its mark to the right with the handles toward the robot. Start with both grippers open in the ready pose.
scoring:
For 0.5, finish with the funnel seated and both flanges clamped. The gap at the low edge must be within 3 mm of zero, the flange centres within 4 mm of each other and their axes within 5 degrees. Both jaws must be between -0.5 and 7 degrees open. The clamp centre must be within 5 mm horizontally and 4 mm vertically of the joint, with no more than 7 degrees of tilt.

For 1.0, also start the lift with the assembled flask resting on its mark, with the foot centre within 4 mm horizontally of the mark. From takeoff through the hold, both pads of the same gripper must hold the upper cylinder. The other arm must stay off the funnel. Both arms must stay off the flask, base and clamp. Hold the lowest edge of the flask foot from 20 mm (top of the blue stripe) to 26 mm (gauge top), inclusive, above its resting surface for 1 s continuously. Set the flask down with the foot centre within 4 mm horizontally of the mark. If the joint comes apart or the flask touches down outside that tolerance, complete a new lift from the mark to earn 1.0. Release the funnel and move both arms clear. For 0.5 s, keep the foot centre within 4 mm horizontally of the mark, the flask within 3 degrees of upright and the foot within 2 mm of its resting surface. Both arms must stay off all parts during that interval. Each gripper's fingertip centre must be at least 100 mm horizontally from the flask axis or at least 50 mm above the funnel top.

For both bench credit levels, film the empty flask in the padded tray with raised sides at setup and over the tray's catch area from takeoff through set-down in every lift attempt. Film from the side during each lift with the foot's lowest edge, the blue stripe and the gauge top in view. Score the final assembly from footage taken before opening the clamp. After every trial with intact glass, including assembly-only trials, film the membrane as you uncover it. Show its whole face and edge against the frit before touching it. Award 0.5 or 1.0 only if the membrane is still centred on the frit and its whole face and edge are free of tears and punctures. Broken glass, a flask outside the tray's catch area during a lift, membrane damage or displacement, or missing or inconclusive required footage earns 0 on the bench.

An incomplete assembly earns 0. Raising the lowest edge of the foot above 26 mm permanently sets the score to 0, even after a valid hold. A trial also earns 0 if the flask tilts past 10 degrees or its foot centre moves more than 30 mm horizontally from the start, the funnel tilts past 45 degrees or drops more than 50 mm below the bench, or the clamp tilts past 60 degrees, drops more than 50 mm below the bench, or drops below 20 mm above the bench while more than 50 mm horizontally from its start.
reset_notes: After a physical trial and its membrane inspection, put a fresh, dry membrane at the centre of the frit. Return the flask to its mark, the funnel to its wipe and the closed clamp to its mark. Open both grippers and return them to the ready pose.
fidelity: The scores refer to the scripted and Dream-1 recordings of the source tree listed in validation.json. The simulator uses rigid glass and a fixed membrane. Bench credit is unverified because the supplied evidence lacks footage of the tray at setup and through any lift, and of the exposed membrane face and edge after the trial. See REFERENCE-SPEC.json for bench scoring.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0 (2,400 steps). Scripted demo: 1.0 (1,423 steps).
